# Phase 3 — Domain Layer
## Objective Define domain models, repository interfaces, and use cases. This layer has no Android framework dependencies.
---
## 3.1 — Domain Models
### `User`
**File:** `domain/model/User.kt`
```kotlin package com.example.twitchtest.domain.model
data class User( val id: String, val firstName: String, val lastName: String, val email: String, val thumbnailUrl: String, val largePictureUrl: String ) { val fullName: String get() = "$firstName $lastName" } ```
### `StreamStatus`
**File:** `domain/model/StreamStatus.kt`
```kotlin package com.example.twitchtest.domain.model
enum class StreamStatus { OFFLINE, CONNECTING, ONLINE, RECONNECTING } ```
---
## 3.2 — Repository Interfaces
### `UserRepository`
**File:** `domain/repository/UserRepository.kt`
```kotlin package com.example.twitchtest.domain.repository
import com.example.twitchtest.domain.model.User import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
interface UserRepository { fun getUsers(): Flow<List<User>> fun searchUsers(query: String): Flow<List<User>> suspend fun refreshUsers() } ```
### `StreamKeyRepository`
**File:** `domain/repository/StreamKeyRepository.kt`
```kotlin package com.example.twitchtest.domain.repository
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
interface StreamKeyRepository { fun getStreamKey(): Flow<String?> suspend fun saveStreamKey(key: String) } ```
---
## 3.3 — Use Cases
### `SaveStreamKeyUseCase`
**File:** `domain/usecase/SaveStreamKeyUseCase.kt`
```kotlin package com.example.twitchtest.domain.usecase
import com.example.twitchtest.domain.repository.StreamKeyRepository import javax.inject.Inject
class SaveStreamKeyUseCase @Inject constructor( private val repository: StreamKeyRepository ) { suspend operator fun invoke(key: String) { repository.saveStreamKey(key) } } ```
### `GetStreamKeyUseCase`
**File:** `domain/usecase/GetStreamKeyUseCase.kt`
```kotlin package com.example.twitchtest.domain.usecase
import com.example.twitchtest.domain.repository.StreamKeyRepository import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow import javax.inject.Inject
class GetStreamKeyUseCase @Inject constructor( private val repository: StreamKeyRepository ) { operator fun invoke(): Flow<String?> = repository.getStreamKey() } ```
### `GetViewersUseCase`
**File:** `domain/usecase/GetViewersUseCase.kt`
Returns a `Flow<List<User>>` from the local database (Room). This gives the UI cached data immediately.
```kotlin package com.example.twitchtest.domain.usecase
import com.example.twitchtest.domain.model.User import com.example.twitchtest.domain.repository.UserRepository import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow import javax.inject.Inject
class GetViewersUseCase @Inject constructor( private val repository: UserRepository ) { operator fun invoke(): Flow<List<User>> = repository.getUsers() } ```
### `RefreshViewersUseCase`
**File:** `domain/usecase/RefreshViewersUseCase.kt`
Fetches fresh users from the API and updates the local database.
```kotlin package com.example.twitchtest.domain.usecase
import com.example.twitchtest.domain.repository.UserRepository import javax.inject.Inject
class RefreshViewersUseCase @Inject constructor( private val repository: UserRepository ) { suspend operator fun invoke() { repository.refreshUsers() } } ```
### `SearchViewersUseCase`
**File:** `domain/usecase/SearchViewersUseCase.kt`
Local search by name/email against Room database.
```kotlin package com.example.twitchtest.domain.usecase
import com.example.twitchtest.domain.model.User import com.example.twitchtest.domain.repository.UserRepository import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow import javax.inject.Inject
class SearchViewersUseCase @Inject constructor( private val repository: UserRepository ) { operator fun invoke(query: String): Flow<List<User>> = repository.searchUsers(query) } ```
---
## Design Notes
- All use cases follow the **single-responsibility principle** — one action per use case. - Use cases use `operator fun invoke()` for clean call-site syntax. - `@Inject constructor` allows Hilt to provide these without manual module bindings. - The domain layer depends on **nothing** from Android or data layer (only Kotlin + coroutines).
---
## Checklist
- [ ] `User` data class with `fullName` computed property - [ ] `StreamStatus` enum with all 4 states - [ ] `UserRepository` interface with `getUsers()`, `searchUsers()`, `refreshUsers()` - [ ] `StreamKeyRepository` interface with `getStreamKey()`, `saveStreamKey()` - [ ] `SaveStreamKeyUseCase` implemented - [ ] `GetStreamKeyUseCase` implemented - [ ] `GetViewersUseCase` implemented - [ ] `RefreshViewersUseCase` implemented - [ ] `SearchViewersUseCase` implemented

# Phase 8 — GitHub & Documentation
## Objective Prepare the project for GitHub: add `.gitignore`, `README.md`, initialize the repository, and push.
---
## 8.1 — `.gitignore`
The project should already have a `.gitignore` from Android Studio. Verify it contains:
```gitignore *.iml .gradle /local.properties /.idea/ .DS_Store /build /captures .externalNativeBuild .cxx *.apk *.ap_ *.aab /app/build ```
---
## 8.2 — `README.md`
**File:** `README.md` (project root)
```markdown # TwitchTest — Android Live Streaming App
A simple Android application for live video streaming to Twitch using RTMP.
## Features
- **Live streaming** to Twitch via RTMP (H264 video + AAC audio) - **Camera controls** — switch between front/back cameras - **Microphone controls** — mute/unmute - **Stream status** — Offline / Connecting / Online / Reconnecting - **Broadcast duration** timer - **Viewer list** — simulated viewers from RandomUser API - **Local search** — filter viewers by name/email - **Offline caching** — viewers stored in Room database
## Tech Stack
| Category | Technology | |---|---| | Language | Kotlin | | Min SDK | API 29 | | Architecture | Clean Architecture + MVI | | UI | Jetpack Compose + Material 3 | | DI | Hilt | | Database | Room | | Network | Retrofit + OkHttp | | Streaming | [RootEncoder](https://github.com/pedroSG94/RootEncoder) | | Navigation | Compose Navigation |
## Screens
1. **Stream Configuration** — Enter and save your Twitch stream key 2. **Main Stream** — Camera preview with streaming controls 3. **Viewer List** (Bottom Sheet) — Simulated viewer list with search
## Setup
1. Clone the repository 2. Open in Android Studio 3. Sync Gradle 4. Get your Twitch stream key from [Twitch Dashboard](https://dashboard.twitch.tv/) 5. Run on a physical device (camera required)
## Architecture
``` presentation/ → MVI (State, Intent, ViewModel, Screen) domain/ → Use Cases, Repository interfaces, Models data/ → Room, Retrofit, DataStore, StreamManager di/ → Hilt modules ```
## License
MIT ```
---
## 8.3 — Git Commands
```bash cd /path/to/TwitchTest
# Initialize repo git init git add . git commit -m "Initial commit: Twitch streaming app with Clean Architecture + MVI"
# Create GitHub repo (via GitHub CLI or website), then: git remote add origin https://github.com/<your-username>/TwitchTest.git git branch -M main git push -u origin main ```
---
## 8.4 — Final Verification Checklist
### Build & Run - [ ] Project syncs without errors - [ ] App builds successfully (`./gradlew assembleDebug`) - [ ] App installs and runs on a physical device - [ ] Permissions are requested on first launch of stream screen
### Stream Configuration Screen - [ ] Stream key can be entered - [ ] Stream key is saved to DataStore - [ ] Previously saved key loads on re-open - [ ] Navigation to Main Stream works after saving key
### Main Stream Screen - [ ] Camera preview displays correctly - [ ] Front/back camera switch works - [ ] Microphone mute/unmute works - [ ] Start stream connects via RTMP to Twitch - [ ] Status shows Connecting → Online - [ ] Duration timer counts while Online - [ ] Stop stream changes status to Offline - [ ] Clicking info panel while Online opens viewer bottom sheet
### Viewer List Bottom Sheet - [ ] Shows cached viewers immediately - [ ] Fetches fresh viewers from RandomUser API - [ ] Updates Room database with new viewers - [ ] Search filters viewers by name/email - [ ] Empty search shows all viewers
### Edge Cases - [ ] App handles no internet gracefully - [ ] Invalid stream key shows error - [ ] Screen stays on during streaming - [ ] Stream stops when app is destroyed
---
## Project Summary
| Metric | Count | |---|---| | Kotlin files | ~30-35 | | Screens | 2 + 1 bottom sheet | | Hilt modules | 4 | | Room entities | 1 | | Use cases | 5 | | Repositories | 2 |
